recorded.prompt:q-session-racy-reference:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-session-racy-reference:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-session-racy-reference:a: Opening section: 'with no edge between those writes and the request thread's reads, the JLS lets the request thread see the reference without the fields.' Summary: 'Without an edge, a reader may get the reference and see the object's fields at their defaults.' Program order on the writer alone is not enough.
recorded.prompt:q-session-racy-reference:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-session-racy-reference:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-session-racy-reference:c: 'The JLS makes every read and write of a reference atomic (JLS 17.7)... That says nothing about the object behind it.' Summary: 'An atomic reference write is not a safe handoff.'
recorded.prompt:q-session-racy-reference:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-session-racy-reference:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-session-racy-reference:d: Reference table (JLS 17.5): 'a plain field of the same object | none'; the final field is the one guaranteed. 'The guarantee extends to the objects and arrays reached through a final field' refutes 'final reference can be read before its target'. The page does not discuss long write atomicity, but it does not need to in order to refute the option.

recorded.pass:q-signing-keys-initializer:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-signing-keys-initializer:b: 'the first caller gets ExceptionInInitializerError, and every later use ... gets NoClassDefFoundError'; reference table 'every later use: NoClassDefFoundError'. PARTLY TRUE: the first call does get ExceptionInInitializerError, and the page says on Java 21 the NoClassDefFoundError's 'cause names the first exception', so 'keeps the first failure' is loosely true; only the exception type for later calls is wrong.

recorded.pass:q-batcher-starts-thread:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-batcher-starts-thread:a: final guarantee 'covers only what the constructor wrote before it finished', lost by 'a constructor that hands out this before it finishes'; reference table 'any field, if the reader saw this before the constructor finished | none'; Summary: 'A constructor that lets this escape gives up that guarantee'.
recorded.prompt:q-batcher-starts-thread:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-batcher-starts-thread:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-batcher-starts-thread:b: Reference table: 'writes before Thread.start() | the started thread | JLS 17.4.4'; 'gives it an edge for the writes before start()' - not only the Thread's own state. PARTLY TRUE: the conclusion 'Possibly 0' and the premise 'start() ran before maxBatch was set' are right; only the stated reason is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-batcher-starts-thread:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-batcher-starts-thread:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-batcher-starts-thread:c: 'an edge for the writes before start() only ..., not for the assignments after it'. PARTLY TRUE: start() does publish the constructor's writes made before it (e.g. this.flusher); it fails only for maxBatch, assigned after start().
